title: Thomas Tuchel says England attackers not producing numbers ‘we would normally expect’
content:
Thomas Tuchel has told England’s attacking players — apart from Harry Kane — that their attacking numbers have fallen below expectations this season.

England will play Japan at Wembley on Tuesday night, their last game before Tuchel decides his squad for the World Cup. After a 1-1 draw with Uruguay on Friday, it will be a stronger England team after some of the leading players — including Kane, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers — joined up with the squad on Saturday.

But Tuchel has warned all of his attacking players, with the exception of his captain Kane, that they have not delivered the numbers of goals and assists this season that he was hoping for.

Speaking at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Monday, Tuchel was asked why he thought England struggled to create scoring chances in their games against top teams. Before their 1-1 draw with Uruguay their only other game against a top-20 ranked team under Tuchel was a friendly against Senegal last June which they lost 3-1.

“I understand the point,” Tuchel said. “I love my players. I really love the quality of our players, especially the offensive players. But the numbers, the pure numbers of our players on the wing and wherever — except for Harry — are not the outstanding numbers we would normally expect. So what is the reason for that? Is it according to the league, that the defenders are so strong that it’s difficult, it’s difficult to score and assist?”

Kane has had another bumper season, with 31 Bundesliga goals and 48 in all competitions so far for Bayern Munich. But for the rest of England’s attacking players it has not been so productive.

“I would love them to have more numbers,” Tuchel said. “Meaning Bukayo (Saka), Noni (Madueke), Ebs (Eberechi Eze), Anthony Gordon, even Cole Palmer, even Morgan Rogers. Not Jude (Bellingham) but Phil Foden. Who is producing, like Harry, these outstanding numbers? Who’s deciding games?”

So far this season, in the Premier League, Palmer has nine goals, Rogers and Jarrod Bowen eight, Foden seven, Saka, Gordon and Eze six each, and Madueke two. Bowen has six Premier League assists, Rogers five, Foden and Saka three each, Gordon and Eze two and Madueke and Palmer one each.
